quest.title: Phantom of the Past
quest.description: The weather is starting to get hot. Paimon wants to buy some fruit juice from Dawn Winery to cool off...

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Good day to you both. It's been quite a long time. You're looking well, as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi, Adelinde!

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: To what do we owe the honor today? Important business to discuss with Master Diluc, I presume?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. Adelinde, since we've run into you, maybe we could just get you to help us with this one?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We always miss the Winery's discount grape juice, so this time we decided to come here early...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can you reserve a bottle for us? We'll pay a deposit, just name the price!

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Of course I can, and no deposit necessary!

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: But I'm afraid you may be in for quite a wait. Dawn Winery's discount grape juice takes a long time to make.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Every summer, Master Diluc hand-picks two barrels of the finest grapes to turn into juice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Why sell the good stuff at a low price? Shouldn't the best grapes be the most expensive?

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Master has never explained his reasoning. If I had to guess...

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: The discount could be a marketing technique. Special deals always attract customers.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Perhaps Master hopes to increase the popularity of fruit juice, so that people have more options when it comes to drinking.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: It makes an ideal alternative for the heaviest drinkers, because they won't get drunk and start causing mischief. At the same time, those who don't drink alcohol get the chance to try something new.

choices.text: Wouldn't that harm the Winery's business...?

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Master Diluc isn't all about money. I think he would prefer to see people drinking in moderation than chase bigger profits at any cost.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Imagine if everyone could just enjoy a nice glass of wine and have a good time while keeping their wits about them and not creating trouble for others... Now wouldn't that be a miracle?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Master Diluc's such a thoughtful guy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, is Diluc picking out this year's grapes right now?

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Not just yet. He has a few more issues to sort out first. He'll start the process as soon as those are out of the way.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: If you're interested, I'm sure Master Diluc would be delighted to see you and hear your thoughts.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What "issues"?

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: As you know, whenever Master Diluc catches wind of any unsavory guests showing up in Mondstadt, he takes it upon himself to go and, ahem, "greet" them in person. It's the same story today.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: He should be somewhere near Falcon Coast. I'm not sure how long he'll be... In the meantime, would you like to take a seat inside?

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: I have to stay here and wait for some other guests, but Hillie and Moco will be glad to take care of you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Unsavory guests"? What is that supposed to mean...?

choices.text: Guessing it has something to do with Diluc's part-time job.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You mean the Darkn—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhhhh... the dark 'n' evil Abyss Order are up to no good again?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case — Master Diluc's our friend, we can't sit here and do nothing!

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: If you're happy to help, that would be wonderful. Master trusts you, after all, and you're both very capable.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: I know he'd appreciate a helping hand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No biggie! The sooner Master Diluc is free, the sooner we can get a taste of that delicious grape juice, hehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Come on, {NICKNAME}, let's go to the Falcon Coast!

choices.text: Alright, we'll wait inside until Diluc gets back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ummm... But Paimon will feel kinda bad if we're sitting in Diluc's house twiddling our thumbs while he's out there hard at work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go to Falcon Coast and help Diluc sort out his issues.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Although Diluc is super strong, surely he'd appreciate a little support.

choices.text: It still doesn't sound like the most profitable venture.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ha... This tent doesn't look like it belongs to Diluc. Maybe it's an adventurer camp?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, there's a piece of paper and a notebook over there. Let's read them.

dialogues.speaker: Someone's Notes
dialogues.text: "Dear Darknight Hero, we are seeing a repeat of the phenomenon we encountered many years ago."

dialogues.speaker: Someone's Notes
dialogues.text: "Although you fully resolved the issue last time, the ley lines seem to have been stimulated in some way and are releasing the monsters they recorded once more."

dialogues.speaker: Someone's Notes
dialogues.text: "I'm sure you'll want to deal with those that pose the biggest threat immediately."

dialogues.speaker: Someone's Notes
dialogues.text: "So I'm notifying essential individuals, per the operating procedures."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... judging by the tone, it seems like this was written by someone Diluc knows well. Let's call him "Diluc's friend" for now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He saw something bad happen, wrote a note for Master Diluc, and then left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Isn't that pretty irresponsible? What if someone else had seen it? Also, he left his notebook behind...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mmm... Now that Paimon thinks about it... you know that strange ley line deposit on the beach?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I bet that's the "phenomenon" he was talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Other than that, everything seems fine here... not a monster in sight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you wanna read Diluc's friend's notebook, too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If not, let's head over and take a closer look at the ley line deposit.

talks.objective: Investigate the abnormal Ley Line deposit

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Where did all these monsters come from!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh.. Wait a second... Is that Diluc?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... He looks kinda different than usual...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look at him go! So focused and full of energy! So this is Captain Pyro when he's in top form, huh!

choices.text: It must be Diluc from when he fought here in the past.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you're right! Now that Paimon looks more closely, this Diluc does look younger than usual.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what happened back then? Why was he fighting here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. Guess we can just ask him about it when we see him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What should we do now, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, let's see how young Diluc used to fight.

choices.text: The ley lines are showing the scene they recorded at that time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The fight is over. Diluc wiped the floor with them... Guess some things haven't changed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So is there any actual danger here? It looks like it's only these illusions from the past.

choices.text: Diluc must have already been here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, Diluc's already called it a day?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Will more monsters come out if we go up to that weird ley line deposit again? And what about young Diluc?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If it's like the other ley line deposits we've seen, then it should've disappeared now that all the monsters are defeated.

choices.text: So young Diluc's piqued your interest?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no, hehe, Paimon's just a little worried is all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What if someone passing by gets curious, comes to check it out, then suddenly "Yaah!" A monster jumps out and clubs him over the head with a "swish" and a "smash"? That would be terrible.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Why the sound effects?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Because it sounds more dangerous that way!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, we came here to help Diluc, didn't we? So let's stick around a little longer and make sure this place is completely safe before we head back.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You've got a strong sense of responsibility.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe... Not really. Paimon just wants some fancy grape juice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Come on, {NICKNAME}, let's finish what we came for. When we get the grape juice, you can have some of Paimon's half!

choices.text: Or have you suddenly developed an interest in ley line anomalies?
At most, there might be a few remnants left.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Please send Master Diluc my regards when you find him.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Also, do be careful out there.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: As Master always says, "Even when the odds of success are nine to one, you must never lower your guard."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that a camp over there? Diluc is camping out in the wild!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... This is weird... Hmm... Maybe these enemies are really tough, and it's turned into a long, drawn-out battle?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go check it out!
